title: Harborland trims growth forecast as exports cool
body: Harborland's independent Budget Office lowered its 2027 growth forecast to 1.4% from 1.8%, citing weaker machinery exports and slower household spending. The office said the estimate assumes no change to the current tax schedule. Finance Minister Lena Voss said the government would publish a revised budget outlook next month. The figures are forecasts, not observed growth.

title: Central bank holds rate, flags sticky services prices
body: The fictional Central Bank of Bellmare kept its policy rate at 3.25% for a fourth meeting. Governor Ivo Marin said services inflation remained above target even as goods prices eased. The bank's statement projected inflation at 2.6% next year, conditional on energy prices and wages. Two committee members preferred a 25 basis point cut, according to the published minutes.

title: Ports reach wage deal after three days of talks
body: Dockworkers at Bellmare's two largest ports accepted a two-year agreement offering a 4.2% pay rise in the first year and 3.0% in the second. The Port Employers Council estimates the agreement covers 8,600 workers. Union representatives said the deal also creates a joint safety committee. The settlement avoids a planned 24-hour stoppage; it does not change port fees.

title: Factory investment grant draws more applicants than expected
body: The Ministry of Industry said 12,400 manufacturing jobs were represented in applications for its new equipment grant. The ministry received 310 applications requesting 96 million crowns, against a 60 million crown budget. It has not selected recipients. A separate estimate from the Manufacturers Forum puts the jobs represented at 14,100, because it counts subcontractor positions as well. The two counts use different definitions and are not directly comparable.

title: Households save more as food bills remain elevated
body: Bellmare's statistics agency reported that the household saving rate rose to 7.1% of disposable income in the third quarter, from 6.5% in the previous quarter. Food prices were 3.8% higher than a year earlier. Economists interviewed by the journal said precautionary saving may explain part of the increase, though the release does not identify household motives.

title: Solar auction clears at lower price than spring round
body: A government auction awarded contracts for 420 megawatts of solar capacity for a weighted average price of 48 crowns per megawatt-hour, 9% below the April round. The energy regulator said projects must begin operating by the end of 2028. The price is a contract bid, not the retail electricity tariff paid by households.

title: Tourism receipts recover, but visitor nights lag
body: Tourism receipts in Bellmare reached 2.3 billion crowns across the opening nine months of 2026, rising 6% in nominal terms against the prior year. The Tourism Board counted 18.2 million overnight stays, still 4% below the same period in 2019. The board cautioned that higher room prices contributed to the receipts increase.

title: River district loan scheme targets small exporters
body: Bellmare's development bank opened a 40 million crown credit line for small firms that export at least 10% of their sales. Loans will be capped at 500,000 crowns per firm, with applications assessed by participating banks. The programme runs through June 2027 or until funds are allocated. The ministry says the facility is a loan guarantee programme, not a direct grant.

title: Hafenland senkt Wachstumsprognose wegen schwächerer Exporte
body: Das unabhängige Haushaltsbüro Hafenlands senkte seine Wachstumsprognose für 2027 von 1,8 auf 1,4 Prozent. Als Gründe nannte es schwächere Maschinenexporte und einen langsameren privaten Konsum. Die Schätzung setzt unveränderte Steuersätze voraus. Finanzministerin Lena Voss kündigte für den kommenden Monat einen aktualisierten Haushaltsausblick an. Es handelt sich um eine Prognose, nicht um bereits gemessenes Wachstum.

title: Havenland verlaagt groeiverwachting door afkoelende export
body: Het onafhankelijke begrotingsbureau van Havenland heeft de groeiverwachting voor 2027 verlaagd van 1,8 naar 1,4 procent. Het noemt zwakkere machine-export en tragere consumptie als oorzaken. De raming gaat uit van ongewijzigde belastingen. Minister van Financiën Lena Voss zei dat de regering volgende maand een herziene begrotingsprognose publiceert. Het gaat om een prognose, niet om gerealiseerde groei.

title: Zentralbank hält Leitzins bei 3,25 Prozent
body: Die fiktive Zentralbank von Bellmare beließ ihren Leitzins zum vierten Mal in Folge bei 3,25 Prozent. Gouverneur Ivo Marin verwies auf anhaltend hohe Dienstleistungspreise, während Warenpreise nachließen. Die Bank prognostiziert für das kommende Jahr eine Inflation von 2,6 Prozent, abhängig von Energiepreisen und Löhnen. Laut veröffentlichtem Protokoll sprachen sich zwei Mitglieder für eine Senkung um 25 Basispunkte aus.

title: Centrale bank houdt rente op 3,25 procent
body: De fictieve centrale bank van Bellmare liet de beleidsrente voor de vierde vergadering op rij op 3,25 procent. Gouverneur Ivo Marin zei dat de prijzen van diensten hoog bleven, terwijl goederen goedkoper werden. De bank verwacht volgend jaar een inflatie van 2,6 procent, afhankelijk van energieprijzen en lonen. Volgens de gepubliceerde notulen wilden twee commissieleden de rente met 25 basispunten verlagen.

title: New rail timetable cuts freight delays at eastern border
body: The state rail operator introduced coordinated freight slots at the eastern border crossing. It expects average waiting times to fall from 11 hours to 7 hours, based on a six-week pilot. The operator said passenger services are unaffected. The forecast depends on neighboring rail networks using the same booking window.

title: Cooperative lenders report rise in late farm payments
body: A survey by Bellmare's Cooperative Lenders Association found that 5.4% of farm loans were more than 30 days overdue in October, compared with 4.1% a year earlier. Lenders pointed to higher fertilizer and feed costs. The association's survey covers its member institutions and is not a national banking statistic. The Agriculture Ministry said a seasonal support payment is due in December.
